facts.title: C²KV: Compressed and Composable KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Inference
facts.event_hint: C²KV proposes learned compressed, position-agnostic KV blocks for non-prefix document reuse
facts.problem: Existing non-prefix KV-cache reuse reduces repeated prefill computation but still loads large, context-dependent KV states from lower-tier memory. Generic compression cannot simply be stacked onto such reuse because compressed states are not designed to remain valid when documents are reordered or concatenated, causing large quality losses.
facts.mechanism: C²KV attaches a lightweight trainable C²Extractor to a frozen base LLM. It inserts one learnable C²Token per block of k document tokens and uses separate per-layer QKV projections only for those tokens. A structured attention mask keeps original-token computation unchanged, lets each C²Token aggregate its local block and sink block, and permits causal accumulation across earlier C²Tokens. Only the resulting compressed KV pairs are stored. At reuse time, independently extracted document KVs receive new positional alignment/RoPE according to their placement and are concatenated directly, without blending or recomputing the original documents. The extractor is trained end-to-end on answers after multi-document KV concatenation, forcing its compressed representation to remain useful under varying document orders and compositions.

evidence.claim: The paper reports up to 17× inference speedup while reducing KV storage and transfer cost and preserving generation quality.
evidence.condition: long-context inference with reusable document KV caches; the headline result is reported by the authors without a single table cell specifying the maximizing workload

evidence.claim: At 128k context on Llama3.1-8B, loading full KV states takes 0.839 seconds while the blending component is 0.132 seconds, supporting the paper's claim that cache movement can dominate reuse preparation.
evidence.baseline: full-size non-prefix reused KV loading and blending

evidence.claim: With 4× compression on Llama3.1-8B, C²KV reaches 0.3587 on MuSiQue and 0.4477 on 2WikiMQA, exceeding the full-recompute scores of 0.3198 and 0.4018 on those two tasks, although it trails full recompute on some other datasets.
A single model trained by sampling 4×, 8×, and 16× compression ratios generalizes to an unseen 10× ratio; on Llama3.1-8B it scores 0.3198 on MuSiQue and 0.4310 on 2WikiMQA at 10×.
Naively adding 4× SnapKV compression to existing reuse methods sharply reduces accuracy; for example CacheBlend falls from 0.2970 to 0.0532 on HotpotQA and from 0.2720 to 0.1311 on MuSiQue.

facts.evaluation_context: The C²Extractor is trained for one epoch on 120,000 multi-document QA examples sampled equally from HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, and LongMagpie, with the base LLM frozen and only C²Token embeddings plus per-layer QKV heads trainable. Evaluation covers LongBench QA and summarization tasks on Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, plus Qwen3-14B scaling and RULER contexts from 4k to 64k. Baselines include full recompute, naive reuse, EPIC, CacheBlend, Block-Attention, and SnapKV combinations. TTFT excludes offline document extraction and the short system/query-token prefill; document KVs are loaded from host memory to GPU, so the reported system evaluation is intra-node memory-tier movement rather than WAN transfer.
facts.limitations: The authors explicitly limit the current system to document-level reuse where reusable content is identifiable and extracted offline; online or incremental extraction is future work. Compression is uniform across documents and layers rather than adaptive or content-aware. The extractor adds about 10% parameters for the evaluated Qwen3-4B and Llama3.1-8B models and requires model-specific training, even though the base model stays frozen. The evaluation does not measure WAN RTT, cross-region cache placement, multi-tenant isolation, cache hit rate, or end-to-end P95 latency. Therefore, applying the result to cross-datacenter KV transfer is an inference: compression reduces bytes, but the paper does not establish that this benefit exceeds remote lookup, consistency, or network costs.
facts.project_relevance: For the cross-region project, C²KV is relevant as evidence that KV transfer optimization may require representations co-designed for later composition, not just generic token eviction or quantization. A useful prototype would compare full KV, generic compressed KV, and composable compressed KV under actual WAN bandwidth/RTT, measuring transferred bytes, cache hit rate, TTFT/P95, extraction amortization, and quality after arbitrary document reordering. Its direct-concatenation and position-realignment mechanism is especially relevant to a distributed document-cache service, but the current paper alone does not validate cross-region economics.
source_notes: Primary source is the KDD 2026 paper/arXiv v1 with DOI and a public code link.

The headline 17× speedup is stated in the abstract and contribution summary, but the extracted text does not expose the exact maximizing workload as a table entry; retain that qualifier in downstream writing.
All reported transfer timings concern host-memory-to-GPU loading, not WAN or cross-region networking.
